opportunities.title: FortiMail Zero-Day: Patch Now, Ask Questions Later (Unauthenticated File Write in the Wild)
opportunities.why_now: Fortinet, SecurityWeek, and The Hacker News all confirm active exploitation of a critical unauthenticated arbitrary file-write bug in FortiMail as of Oct 2.
opportunities.angle: Rapid-patch advisory digest: CVE details, exploitation timeline, who's already been hit, and a blunt 'patch today' checklist.

opportunities.title: Dual NetScaler Zero-Days: Citrix's Worst Week Since the Last Worst Week
opportunities.why_now: Dark Reading reports two simultaneous zero-days in Citrix NetScaler causing active chaos for customers.
opportunities.angle: Breach-digest style: stack this against Citrix's history of zero-day incidents to argue 'inevitable' pattern, with patch-cadence timeline graphic.

opportunities.title: Microsoft Caught Hackers Exploiting Zimbra Before Anyone Even Knew the Bug Existed
opportunities.why_now: Confirmed pre-disclosure exploitation of a Zimbra vuln, reported by both The Register and SecurityWeek on Oct 1.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor deep dive: how attackers beat the disclosure clock, what it means for 'patch Tuesday' assumptions, and why pre-disclosure exploitation is the new normal.

opportunities.title: Warlock Ransomware Goes Industrial: SharePoint Exploits Now Hitting Critical Infrastructure
opportunities.why_now: SecurityWeek's Oct 2 report shows Warlock expanding from Spanish/Portuguese orgs into critical infrastructure via SharePoint flaws.
opportunities.angle: Ransomware tracker entry: map Warlock's victim expansion, tie back to unpatched SharePoint CVEs, and list exposed sectors.

opportunities.title: AI Agents Are Now Hacking the Hackers (and Government Sites) — Autonomous Attacks Have Arrived
opportunities.why_now: Two fresh stories — AI agents breaching a security research org's email data and AI agents launching SQLi against US/Canadian government sites — show autonomous AI attack tooling going mainstream in the same week.
opportunities.angle: Trend digest combining both incidents into one 'the bots are attacking now' piece, with implications for SOC patch/response speed.
